steps.message: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

The game works, and now we want prizes.

The quiz settings get a new field, "Number of winners" (a number, at least 1, 3 by default).

Scoring:

- Each correct answer gives one point.
- Players with equal points are ranked by speed: the total time of their correct answers wins when it is lower. The time of an answer runs from the moment the question opens to the player's last pick.
- Players don't see points during the game.

Speed now decides ties, so all players must get each question at the same moment: the big screen and the phones must follow the moderator close to instantly.

After "End quiz":

- The big screen shows the leaderboard: one list item for each player, in order, with the place, the name, and the points ("2 points", "1 point", "0 points").
- Each player's phone shows the place ("Place 2 of 5") and the points ("3 points").

Picking the winners (N is the number of winners):

- The "Top N" button (for example, "Top 3") makes the first N players of the leaderboard the winners.
- The "Draw" button is for ties. Every player with more points than the N-th place wins. The remaining prizes are drawn at random among the players with exactly the N-th place's points (speed doesn't matter here). Each click draws again.
- Players with 0 points never win. If fewer than N players have points, all of them win.
- The "Reset winners" button removes the winners.
- Winners get the "Winner" mark on the leaderboard, and their phones show "You won!". Both update live.

  "output_head": "# Quizzy Architecture & Design Notes

## Overview
Quizzy is a Rails 8.1 application (SQLite + Propshaft + Hotwire/Stimulus + Action Cable/Solid Cable) for running live conference talk quizzes.

## Runtime & Deployment (`bin/serve`)
- Started via `bin/serve` with `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- Plain HTTP (`assume_ssl = false`, `force_ssl = false`), accepts any `Host` header (`config.hosts.clear`), serves static assets directly from Puma (`public_file_server.enabled = true`).
- Health check at `GET /up` (unauthenticated, returns `200`).
- All SQLite databases (`primary`, `cache`, `queue`, `cable`) reside under `storage/`.

## Domain Model
### Quiz Preparation
- `Quiz` (`quizzes`): `title` (required). `has_many :questions` ordered by `(position, id)`, `has_many :active_questions`, `has_many :games`.
- `Question` (`questions`): `quiz_id`, `body` (required), `active` (boolean, default `true`), `position` (1-indexed integer). `has_many :options` ordered by `(position, id)`.
  - `save_with_option_rows(question_attrs, raw_rows)`: skips blank option rows, validates `>= 2` non-empty options (`"Add at least two options"`) and `>= 1` correct option among non-empty rows (`"Mark at least one option as correct"`). On failure, rolls back / avoids DB writes and preserves exact user-entered rows on `@question.form_option_rows`.
  - `move_up!` / `move_down!`: swaps adjacent siblings inside `quiz.with_lock` and compacts positions `1..n`.
- `Option` (`options`): `question_id`, `text` (required), `correct` (boolean, default `false`), `position` (1-indexed integer). Multiple correct options per question are supported.

### Live Game
- `Game` (`games`): `quiz_id`, unique 5-char uppercase `code` (e.g. `K7RZX`), `status` (`lobby` -> `question_open` <-> `question_closed` -> `finished`), `current_question_index`, monotonic `state_version`, `base_url`, timestamps (`started_at`, `question_opened_at`, `question_closed_at`, `finished_at`).
  - `start!` snapshots `@quiz.active_questions` (skipping inactive questions) and their `options` into `GameQuestion` (`game_questions`) and `GameOption` (`game_options`), isolating the running/completed game from future quiz edits while keeping optional `question_id` / `option_id` references (`on_delete: :nullify`).
  - Inline SVG QR code is generated locally via `rqrcode` (`Game#qr_svg`) encoding the exact same `join_url` displayed on the lobby screen.
- `Player` (`players`): `game_id`, `name` (required), `token` (unique), `browser_token` (unique per `game_id`, persisted in permanent signed cookies so reopening `/play/:code` in the same browser resumes as the same player while other games remain independent), `connections_count`, `online_until`.
  - `Player.currently_online` tracks players currently connected via `PlayGameChannel` WebSocket (`connections_count > 0`) or within a short HTTP grace window (`online_until > Time.current`) for initial page load and conference Wi-Fi HTTP fallback polling; `pagehide` beacon (`POST /play/:code/leave`) + WebSocket `unsubscribed` immediately mark disconnected tabs offline.
- `GameAnswer` (`game_answers`): unique per `(game_question_id, player_id)`, pointing to `game_option_id`, `client_seq`, and `answered_at`. Players can change their pick while `question_open?`; `client_seq` prevents delayed out-of-order conference Wi-Fi packets from overwriting a newer pick.

## Real-Time Channels & Security
- `ModerateGameChannel`: authenticates via HMAC-signed `stream_token` (`Rails.application.message_verifier(:moderate_game)`), streaming live state and player/answer counters to the moderator's big screen (`moderator_game_controller.js`).
- `PlayGameChannel`: streams public game state (`play_game_<code>`) and player-specific answer confirmations (`play_player_<token>`) to audience phones (`play_controller.js`).
- **Answer secrecy invariant**: While `status == "question_open"`, neither HTML source, JSON state endpoints, nor WebSocket broadcasts include option `correct` flags anywhere. `correct` booleans are only serialized once `finish_question!` transitions the game to `question_closed`.
- Both `moderator_game_controller.js` and `play_controller.js` combine Action Cable WebSockets with monotonic-versioned state reconciliation and lightweight background sync/retry for resilience on crowded conference Wi-Fi without page reloads.

## Moderator Area (`/moderate`)
- All controllers under `Moderate::` inherit from `Moderate::BaseController`, which enforces HTTP Basic Auth against `ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME"]` and `ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD"]` using `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`.
- Live game moderation lives at `/moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/games/:id` (`Moderate::GamesController`).

## Quiz Export & Import
- **Export** (`GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/export` -> `Quiz#export_payload` / `Quiz#to_export_json`): writes **only** `title` and `questions` (`text`, `active`, `options` -> `tex",

  "output": "# Quizzy Architecture & Design Notes

## Overview
Quizzy is a Rails 8.1 application (SQLite + Propshaft + Hotwire/Stimulus + Action Cable/Solid Cable) for running live conference talk quizzes.

## Runtime & Deployment (`bin/serve`)
- Started via `bin/serve` with `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- Plain HTTP (`assume_ssl = false`, `force_ssl = false`), accepts any `Host` header (`config.hosts.clear`), serves static assets directly from Puma (`public_file_server.enabled = true`).
- Health check at `GET /up` (unauthenticated, returns `200`).
- All SQLite databases (`primary`, `cache`, `queue`, `cable`) reside under `storage/`.

## Domain Model
### Quiz Preparation
- `Quiz` (`quizzes`): `title` (required). `has_many :questions` ordered by `(position, id)`, `has_many :active_questions`, `has_many :games`.
- `Question` (`questions`): `quiz_id`, `body` (required), `active` (boolean, default `true`), `position` (1-indexed integer). `has_many :options` ordered by `(position, id)`.
  - `save_with_option_rows(question_attrs, raw_rows)`: skips blank option rows, validates `>= 2` non-empty options (`"Add at least two options"`) and `>= 1` correct option among non-empty rows (`"Mark at least one option as correct"`). On failure, rolls back / avoids DB writes and preserves exact user-entered rows on `@question.form_option_rows`.
  - `move_up!` / `move_down!`: swaps adjacent siblings inside `quiz.with_lock` and compacts positions `1..n`.
- `Option` (`options`): `question_id`, `text` (required), `correct` (boolean, default `false`), `position` (1-indexed integer). Multiple correct options per question are supported.

### Live Game
- `Game` (`games`): `quiz_id`, unique 5-char uppercase `code` (e.g. `K7RZX`), `status` (`lobby` -> `question_open` <-> `question_closed` -> `finished`), `current_question_index`, monotonic `state_version`, `base_url`, timestamps (`started_at`, `question_opened_at`, `question_closed_at`, `finished_at`).
  - `start!` snapshots `@quiz.active_questions` (skipping inactive questions) and their `options` into `GameQuestion` (`game_questions`) and `GameOption` (`game_options`), isolating the running/completed game from future quiz edits while keeping optional `question_id` / `option_id` references (`on_delete: :nullify`).
  - Inline SVG QR code is generated locally via `rqrcode` (`Game#qr_svg`) encoding the exact same `join_url` displayed on the lobby screen.
- `Player` (`players`): `game_id`, `name` (required), `token` (unique), `browser_token` (unique per `game_id`, persisted in permanent signed cookies so reopening `/play/:code` in the same browser resumes as the same player while other games remain independent), `connections_count`, `online_until`.
  - `Player.currently_online` tracks players currently connected via `PlayGameChannel` WebSocket (`connections_count > 0`) or within a short HTTP grace window (`online_until > Time.current`) for initial page load and conference Wi-Fi HTTP fallback polling; `pagehide` beacon (`POST /play/:code/leave`) + WebSocket `unsubscribed` immediately mark disconnected tabs offline.
- `GameAnswer` (`game_answers`): unique per `(game_question_id, player_id)`, pointing to `game_option_id`, `client_seq`, and `answered_at`. Players can change their pick while `question_open?`; `client_seq` prevents delayed out-of-order conference Wi-Fi packets from overwriting a newer pick.

## Real-Time Channels & Security
- `ModerateGameChannel`: authenticates via HMAC-signed `stream_token` (`Rails.application.message_verifier(:moderate_game)`), streaming live state and player/answer counters to the moderator's big screen (`moderator_game_controller.js`).
- `PlayGameChannel`: streams public game state (`play_game_<code>`) and player-specific answer confirmations (`play_player_<token>`) to audience phones (`play_controller.js`).
- **Answer secrecy invariant**: While `status == "question_open"`, neither HTML source, JSON state endpoints, nor WebSocket broadcasts include option `correct` flags anywhere. `correct` booleans are only serialized once `finish_question!` transitions the game to `question_closed`.
- Both `moderator_game_controller.js` and `play_controller.js` combine Action Cable WebSockets with monotonic-versioned state reconciliation and lightweight background sync/retry for resilience on crowded conference Wi-Fi without page reloads.

## Moderator Area (`/moderate`)
- All controllers under `Moderate::` inherit from `Moderate::BaseController`, which enforces HTTP Basic Auth against `ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME"]` and `ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD"]` using `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`.
- Live game moderation lives at `/moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/games/:id` (`Moderate::GamesController`).

## Quiz Export & Import
- **Export** (`GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/export` -> `Quiz#export_payload` / `Quiz#to_export_json`): writes **only** `title` and `questions` (`text`, `active`, `options` -> `text`, `correct`), unaffected by games, players, or answers.
- **Import** (`GET/POST /moderate/quizzes/import` -> `Quiz::Import`): validates and atomically creates a new `Quiz`.

class Quiz::Import
  attr_reader :raw_json, :quiz, :errors

  def initialize(raw_json = "")
    @raw_json = raw_json.to_s
    @errors = []
    @quiz = nil
  end

  def save
    @errors = []
    @quiz = nil

    if @raw_json.strip.empty?
      @errors << "Quiz JSON can't be blank"
      return false
    end

    data =
      begin
        JSON.parse(@raw_json)
      rescue JSON::JSONError
        @errors << "Quiz JSON is not valid JSON"
        return false
      end

    unless data.is_a?(Hash)
      @errors << "Quiz JSON must be a JSON object"
      return false
    end

    normalized = validate_and_extract(data)
    return false if @errors.any?

    ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
      created_quiz = Quiz.create!(title: normalized[:title])
      normalized[:questions].each_with_index do |q_attrs, q_idx|
        question = created_quiz.questions.create!(
          body: q_attrs[:text],
          active: q_attrs[:active],
          position: q_idx + 1
        )
        q_attrs[:options].each_with_index do |opt_attrs, opt_idx|
          question.options.create!(
            text: opt_attrs[:text],
            correct: opt_attrs[:correct],
            position: opt_idx + 1
          )
        end
      end
      @quiz = created_quiz
    end

    true
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => e
    @quiz = nil
    @errors << e.record.errors.full_messages.to_sentence
    false
  end

  private

  def validate_and_extract(data)
    title = validate_title(data)
    questions = validate_questions(data)

    { title: title, questions: questions }
  end

  def validate_title(data)
    if !data.key?("title") || data["title"].nil?
      @errors << "Title can't be blank"
      return nil
    end

    unless data["title"].is_a?(String)
      @errors << "Title must be a string"
      return nil
    end

    stripped = data["title"].strip
    if stripped.empty?
      @errors << "Title can't be blank"
      return nil
    end

    stripped
  end

  def validate_questions(data)
    if !data.key?("questions") || !data["questions"].is_a?(Array)
      @errors << "Questions must be an array"
      return []
    end

    data["questions"].each_with_index.map do |q_data, q_idx|
      validate_question(q_data, q_idx + 1)
    end
  end

  def validate_question(q_data, q_num)
    unless q_data.is_a?(Hash)
      @errors << "Question #{q_num} must be an object"
      return nil
    end

    text = validate_question_text(q_data, q_num)
    active = validate_question_active(q_data, q_num)
    options = validate_question_options(q_data, q_num)

    { text: text, active: active, options: options }
  end

  def validate_question_text(q_data, q_num)
    if !q_data.key?("text") || q_data["text"].nil?
      @errors << "Question #{q_num}: Question can't be blank"
      return nil
    end

    unless q_data["text"].is_a?(String)
      @errors << "Question #{q_num}: Question text must be a string"
      return nil
    end

    if q_data["text"].blank?
      @errors << "Question #{q_num}: Question can't be blank"
      return nil
    end

    q_data["text"]
  end

  def validate_question_active(q_data, q_num)
    return true unless q_data.key?("active")

    value = q_data["active"]
    unless value == true || value == false
      @errors << "Question #{q_num}: Active must be true or false"
      return true
    end

    value
  end

  def validate_question_options(q_data, q_num)
    if !q_data.key?("options") || !q_data["options"].is_a?(Array)
      @errors << "Question #{q_num}: Options must be an array"
      return []
    end

    raw_options = q_data["options"]
    parsed_options = raw_options.each_with_index.map do |opt_data, opt_idx|
      validate_option(opt_data, q_num, opt_idx + 1)

    if raw_options.size < 2
      @errors << "Question #{q_num}: Add at least two options"
    elsif parsed_options.compact.size == raw_options.size && parsed_options.none? { |o| o[:correct] }
      @errors << "Question #{q_num}: Mark at least one option as correct"
    end

    parsed_options.compact
  end

  def validate_option(opt_data, q_num, opt_num)

class Question < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy

  validates :body, presence: true

  after_destroy :compact_quiz_positions

  attr_writer :option_rows

  def form_option_rows
    return @option_rows unless @option_rows.nil?

    if persisted?
      loaded = options.order(:position, :id).map { |opt| { text: opt.text, correct: opt.correct? } }
      loaded.presence || default_empty_rows
    else
      default_empty_rows
    end
  end

  def save_with_option_rows(question_attrs, raw_rows)
    rows = normalize_option_rows(raw_rows)
    assign_attributes(question_attrs)

    valid?

    filled_rows = rows.reject { |r| r[:text].strip.empty? }
    if filled_rows.size < 2
      errors.add(:base, "Add at least two options")
    elsif filled_rows.none? { |r| r[:correct] }
      errors.add(:base, "Mark at least one option as correct")
    end

    if errors.any?
      @option_rows = rows
      return false
    end

    Question.transaction do
      if new_record?
        self.position = (quiz.questions.maximum(:position) || 0) + 1
      end
      save!
      options.destroy_all
      filled_rows.each_with_index do |row, idx|
        options.create!(
          text: row[:text].strip,
          correct: row[:correct],
          position: idx + 1
        )
      end
    end

    true
  end

  def move_up!
    quiz.with_lock do
      siblings = quiz.questions.order(:position, :id).to_a
      idx = siblings.index(self)
      return if idx.nil? || idx == 0

      siblings[idx - 1], siblings[idx] = siblings[idx], siblings[idx - 1]
      reindex_siblings!(siblings)
    end
  end

  def move_down!
    quiz.with_lock do
      siblings = quiz.questions.order(:position, :id).to_a
      idx = siblings.index(self)
      return if idx.nil? || idx >= siblings.size - 1

      siblings[idx], siblings[idx + 1] = siblings[idx + 1], siblings[idx]
      reindex_siblings!(siblings)
    end
  end

  private

  def default_empty_rows
    Array.new(4) { { text: "", correct: false } }
  end

  def normalize_option_rows(raw_rows)
    return [] if raw_rows.blank?

    boolean_type = ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new
    entries =
      if raw_rows.respond_to?(:to_unsafe_h)
        raw_rows.to_unsafe_h.sort_by { |k, _| k.to_i }.map(&:last)
      elsif raw_rows.is_a?(Hash)
        raw_rows.sort_by { |k, _| k.to_i }.map(&:last)
      elsif raw_rows.is_a?(Array)
        raw_rows
      else
        []
      end

    entries.map do |entry|
      h = entry.is_a?(Hash) ? entry.with_indifferent_access : {}
      {
        text: h[:text].to_s,
        correct: boolean_type.cast(h[:correct]) || false
      }
    end
  end

  def compact_quiz_positions
    return unless quiz && !quiz.destroyed?

    siblings = quiz.questions.order(:position, :id).to_a
    reindex_siblings!(siblings)
  end

  def reindex_siblings!(siblings)
    siblings.each_with_index do |q, i|
      new_pos = i + 1
      q.update_columns(position: new_pos) if q.position != new_pos
    end
  end
end

class PlayGameChannel < ApplicationCable::Channel
  def subscribed
    code = params[:code].to_s.strip.upcase
    @game = Game.find_by(code: code)
    if @game.nil?
      reject
      return
    end

    stream_from "play_game_#{@game.code}"

    player_token = params[:player_token].to_s
    if player_token.present?
      player = @game.players.find_by(token: player_token)
      if player
        @player = player
        stream_from "play_player_#{@player.token}"
        @player.increment_connections!
      end
    end

    if @player
      transmit(@game.player_state_payload(@player).merge(type: "player_sync"))
    else
      transmit(@game.play_broadcast_payload)
    end
  end

  def unsubscribed
    @player&.decrement_connections!
  end
end

class PlaysController < ApplicationController
  before_action :set_game

  def show
    ensure_browser_token!
    @quiz = @game.quiz
    @player = find_current_player
    if @player && !@game.finished?
      @player.touch_online_grace!
    end
    @initial_state = @game.reload.player_state_payload(@player)
  end

  def join
    @quiz = @game.quiz

    if @game.finished?
      if async_request?
        render json: { joined: false, state: @game.player_state_payload(nil) }, status: :unprocessable_entity
      else
        redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other
      end
      return
    end

    existing_player = find_current_player
    if existing_player
      existing_player.touch_online_grace!
      remember_player!(existing_player)
      if async_request?
        render json: { joined: true, state: @game.reload.player_state_payload(existing_player) }
      else
        redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other
      end
      return
    end

    b_token = ensure_browser_token!
    @player = @game.players.new(
      name: params[:name].to_s,
      browser_token: b_token,
      online_until: Player::ONLINE_GRACE_DURATION.from_now
    )

    begin
      saved = @player.save
    rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
      @player = @game.players.find_by!(browser_token: b_token)
      saved = true
    end

    if saved
      remember_player!(@player)
      @game.bump_version_and_broadcast_moderator!
      if async_request?
        render json: { joined: true, state: @game.reload.player_state_payload(@player) }
      else
        redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other
      end
    else
      @join_error = @player.errors.full_messages.first || "Enter your name"
      if async_request?
        render json: { joined: false, error: @join_error }, status: :unprocessable_entity
      else
        @player = nil
        @initial_state = @game.player_state_payload(nil)
        render :show, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end
    end
  end

  def answer
    @player = find_current_player
    if @player.nil?
      head :unauthorized
      return
    end

    result = @game.submit_answer!(
      player: @player,
      option_id: params[:option_id],
      client_seq: params[:client_seq]
    )

    render json: {
      accepted: result[:accepted],
      state: @game.reload.player_state_payload(@player)
    }
  end

  def state
    @player = find_current_player
    if @player && !@game.finished? && params[:offline_poll] == "1"
      @player.touch_online_grace!
    end
    render json: @game.reload.player_state_payload(@player)
  end

  def leave
    @player = find_current_player
    @player&.clear_online_grace!
    head :no_content
  end

  private

  def set_game
    @game = Game.includes(:quiz).find_by!(code: params[:code].to_s.strip.upcase)
  end

  def async_request?
    request.headers["X-Quizzy-Async"] == "1" || request.format.json?
  end

  def ensure_browser_token!
    existing = cookies.signed[:quizzy_browser_token]
    return existing if existing.present?

    generated = SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(24)
    cookies.permanent.signed[:quizzy_browser_token] = {
      value: generated,
      httponly: true,
      same_site: :lax
    }
    generated
  end

  def player_cookie_key
    :"quizzy_player_#{@game.code}"
  end

  def remember_player!(player)
    cookies.permanent.signed[player_cookie_key] = {
      value: player.token,
      httponly: true,
      same_site: :lax
    }
  end

  def find_current_player
    token = cookies.signed[player_cookie_key].presence || params[:player_token].presence
    if token.present?
      by_token = @game.players.find_by(token: token)
      return by_token if by_token
    end

    b_token = cookies.signed[:quizzy_browser_token]
    @game.players.find_by(browser_token: b_token) if b_token.present?
  end
end

require "test_helper"

class LiveGameHttpAndSecurityTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    @quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Security Conf Quiz")
    @q1 = @quiz.questions.new
    @q1.save_with_option_rows(
      { body: "Secret question?", active: true },
      {
        "0" => { text: "AlphaOption", correct: "0" },
        "1" => { text: "BravoSecretWinner", correct: "1" }
      }
    )
    @game = @quiz.games.create!(base_url: "http://projector.conf.local:3000")
  end

  test "player joins with case-insensitive code, remembered by cookie, and open question leaks nothing about correctness in HTML or JSON" do
    # Case-insensitive join URL works
    get "/play/#{@game.code.downcase}"
    assert_response :success
    assert_includes response.body, "Your name"

    post "/play/#{@game.code.downcase}/join", params: { name: "Eve" }
    assert_redirected_to "/play/#{@game.code}"
    follow_redirect!
    assert_response :success
    assert_includes response.body, "Hi, Eve!"

    # Moderator starts the game
    patch "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/games/#{@game.id}/start", headers: moderator_auth_headers
    assert_redirected_to "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/games/#{@game.id}"

    # Eve reloads /play/:code -> remembered as Eve, sees question, NO 'correct' anywhere in HTML source!
    get "/play/#{@game.code}"
    assert_response :success
    assert_includes response.body, "Secret question?"
    assert_includes response.body, "AlphaOption"
    assert_includes response.body, "BravoSecretWinner"
    refute_match(/correct/i, response.body)

    # /play/:code/state JSON also contains NO 'correct' key while open
    get "/play/#{@game.code}/state"
    assert_response :success
    refute_match(/correct/i, response.body)

    # Moderator finishes question -> now state reveals correctness
    patch "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/games/#{@game.id}/finish", headers: moderator_auth_headers
    get "/play/#{@game.code}/state"
    assert_response :success
    state_json = JSON.parse(response.body)
    assert_equal "question_closed", state_json["status"]
    bravo = state_json.dig("question", "options").find { |o| o["text"] == "BravoSecretWinner" }
    assert_equal true, bravo["correct"]

    # Moderator ends quiz -> new visitor cannot join via GET or POST

For `number_of_winners`, I'll make sure it's a number (specifically, an integer) and greater than or equal to 1. But wait... what happens if someone enters something like "2.5" or "abc"? This is where I have to remember how ActiveRecord deals with type casting. I need to refresh myself on how this impacts validations.

Aha! It looks like ActiveRecord will cast certain values. For example if someone submits "abc", `number_of_winners` will become 0! Since I'm validating based on the *raw* value, I'll need to remember that the `numericality` validator checks the raw value, which means `"abc"` will pass the `presence: true` check because it has been converted to `0`. However, the raw value `"abc"` will raise an error when checked against the `numericality` validation rule.

So, I need to make sure the validations catch all the edge cases: empty strings, strings that can be converted to numbers, non-numeric strings, and numbers outside the valid range. I should probably test all of these cases in `rails runner` to confirm my understanding of the behavior.

Next, `app/models/game_answer.rb`. This one's pretty straightforward: I'll associate it with `game_question`, `player`, and `game_option`. There's also a `before_validation` callback, `compute_response_time_us`, which calculates the response time. I'll need to double-check that the timing calculation is accurate, handles null values properly, and works correctly in all situations. Then, I need to validate the `answered_at` field and ensure `response_time_us` is a non-negative integer.

Finally, `app/models/game.rb`. Here, I'll really scrutinize the game logic. I need to verify:
*   `assign_unique_code` and `assign_number_of_winners` are run correctly before validation.
*   The `start!` method: making sure the number of winners is snapshot and the opened at values are correct
*   The `next_question!` method, ensuring everything is updated as expected.
*   The `end_quiz!`, `pick_top_winners!`, `draw_winners!`, and `reset_winners!` methods are thoroughly reviewed for correctness, especially considering potential concurrency issues. The use of `with_lock` is crucial here to ensure data integrity.
*   The `draw_winners!` method is particularly interesting, since it uses `SecureRandom` for randomness in production but also takes in an optional random to enable seeded tests!

Now, armed with this deeper understanding, I can update the controllers as well, knowing that the models' behaviors are all considered.

cat <<'EOF' > app/models/game_answer.rb
class GameAnswer < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :game_question
  belongs_to :player
  belongs_to :game_option

  before_validation :compute_response_time_us

  validates :answered_at, presence: true
  validates :response_time_us, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0 }

  private

  def compute_response_time_us
    return if answered_at.nil? || (response_time_us.present? && response_time_us > 0)
    return unless game_question

    opened = game_question.opened_at || game_question.game&.question_opened_at
    return if opened.nil?

    elapsed = ((answered_at.to_r - opened.to_r) * 1_000_000).round
    self.response_time_us = [ elapsed, 0 ].max
  end
end
EOF

cat <<'EOF' > app/models/game.rb
class Game < ApplicationRecord
  CODE_ALPHABET = "23456789ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ".chars.freeze
  CODE_LENGTH = 5
  STATUSES = %w[lobby question_open question_closed finished].freeze

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :game_questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :players, dependent: :destroy

  before_validation :assign_unique_code, on: :create
  before_validation :assign_number_of_winners, on: :create

  validates :code, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :status, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }
  validates :number_of_winners, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than_or_equal_to: 1 }

  def self.points_label(points)
    "#{points} #{points == 1 ? 'point' : 'points'}"
  end

  def lobby?
    status == "lobby"
  end

  def question_open?
    status == "question_open"
  end

  def question_closed?
    status == "question_closed"
  end

  def finished?
    status == "finished"
  end

  def current_game_question
    return nil if lobby? || finished?

    game_questions.includes(:game_options).find_by(position: current_question_index + 1)
  end

  def online_player_ids
    players.currently_online.pluck(:id)
  end

  def active_players_count
    players.currently_online.count
  end

  def join_url(fallback_base_url = nil)
    effective_base = fallback_base_url.presence || base_url.presence || "http://localhost:3000"
    "#{effective_base.sub(%r{/\z}, '')}/play/#{code}"
  end

  def qr_svg(fallback_base_url = nil)
    qrcode = RQRCode::QRCode.new(join_url(fallback_base_url))
    qrcode.as_svg(
      color: "000000",
      fill: "ffffff",
      shape_rendering: "crispEdges",
      module_size: 8,
      offset: 16,
      standalone: true,
      use_path: true,
      viewbox: true,
      svg_attributes: {
        role: "img",
        "aria-label" => "QR code"
      }
    ).sub(/\A<\?xml[^?]*\?>\s*/, "").html_safe
  end

  def stream_token
    Rails.application.message_verifier(:moderate_game).generate(id)
  end

  def self.find_by_stream_token(token)
    game_id = Rails.application.message_verifier(:moderate_game).verified(token)
    find_by(id: game_id) if game_id.present?
  end

  def start!
    changed = false
    with_lock do
      next unless lobby?

      quiz_record = Quiz.find(quiz_id)
      winners_n = quiz_record.number_of_winners
      active_qs = quiz_record.active_questions.includes(:options).to_a
      now = Time.current

      if active_qs.empty?
        update!(
          status: "finished",
          number_of_winners: winners_n,
          started_at: now,
          finished_at: now,
          state_version: state_version + 1
        )
      else
        active_qs.each_with_index do |q, q_idx|
          gq = game_questions.create!(
            question_id: q.id,
            body: q.body,
            position: q_idx + 1,
            opened_at: q_idx == 0 ? now : nil
          )
          q.options.each_with_index do |opt, o_idx|
            gq.game_options.create!(
              option_id: opt.id,
              text: opt.text,
              correct: opt.correct?,
              position: o_idx + 1
            )
          end
        end

        update!(
          status: "question_open",
          number_of_winners: winners_n,
          current_question_index: 0,
          started_at: now,
          question_opened_at: now,
          question_closed_at: nil,
          state_version: state_version + 1
        )
      end
      changed = true
    end

    broadcast_all! if changed
    changed
  end

  def finish_question!
    changed = false
    with_lock do
      next unless question_open?

      update!(
        status: "question_closed",
        question_closed_at: Time.current,
        state_version: state_version + 1
      )
      changed = true
    end

    broadcast_all! if changed
    changed
  end

  def next_question!
    changed = false
    with_lock do
      next unless question_closed?

      next_index = current_question_index + 1
      next_gq = game_questions.find_by(position: next_index + 1)
      next if next_gq.nil?

      now = Time.current
      next_gq.update!(opened_at: now)
      update!(
        status: "question_open",
        current_question_index: next_index,
        question_opened_at: now,
        question_closed_at: nil,
        state_version: state_version + 1
      )
      changed = true
    end

    broadcast_all! if changed
    changed
  end

  def end_quiz!
    changed = false
    with_lock do
      next if finished?

      players.where(winner: true).update_all(winner: false)
      update!(
        status: "finished",
        finished_at: Time.current,
        state_version: state_version + 1
      )
      changed = true
    end

    broadcast_all! if changed
    changed
  end

  def pick_top_winners!
    changed = false
    with_lock do
      next unless finished?

      eligible = leaderboard_records.select { |entry| entry[:points] > 0 }
      winner_ids = eligible.first(number_of_winners).map { |entry| entry[:player].id }

      players.update_all(winner: false)
      players.where(id: winner_ids).update_all(winner: true) if winner_ids.any?
      update_columns(state_version: state_version + 1, updated_at: Time.current)
      changed = true
    end

    broadcast_all! if changed
    changed
  end

  def draw_winners!(random: SecureRandom)
    changed = false
    with_lock do
      next unless finished?

      records = leaderboard_records
      eligible = records.select { |entry| entry[:points] > 0 }

      winner_ids =
        if eligible.size <= number_of_winners
          eligible.map { |entry| entry[:player].id }
        else
          cutoff_points = records[number_of_winners - 1][:points]
          guaranteed = eligible.select { |entry| entry[:points] > cutoff_points }
          remaining = number_of_winners - guaranteed.size
          tied_pool = eligible.select { |entry| entry[:points] == cutoff_points }
          drawn = tied_pool.sample(remaining, random: random)
          (guaranteed + drawn).map { |entry| entry[:player].id }
        end

      players.update_all(winner: false)
      players.where(id: winner_ids).update_all(winner: true) if winner_ids.any?
      update_columns(state_version: state_version + 1, updated_at: Time.current)
      changed = true
    end

    broadcast_all! if changed
    changed
  end

  def reset_winners!
    changed = false
    with_lock do
      next unless finished?

      players.where(winner: true).update_all(winner: false)
      update_columns(state_version: state_version + 1, updated_at: Time.current)
      changed = true
    end

    broadcast_all! if changed
    changed
  end

  def submit_answer!(player:, option_id:, client_seq: 0)
    result = nil
    gq = nil

    with_lock do
      if !question_open? || player.nil? || player.game_id != id
        result = { accepted: false }
        next
      end

      gq = current_game_question
      if gq.nil?
        result = { accepted: false }
        next
      end

      option = gq.game_options.find { |o| o.id == option_id.to_i }
      if option.nil?
        result = { accepted: false }
        next
      end

      answer = gq.game_answers.find_or_initialize_by(player_id: player.id)
      seq = client_seq.to_i

      if answer.persisted? && seq > 0 && answer.client_seq > 0 && seq < answer.client_seq
        result = { accepted: true, question_id: gq.id, picked_option_id: answer.game_option_id }
        next
      end

      now = Time.current
      opened_at = gq.opened_at || question_opened_at || now
      elapsed_us = ((now.to_r - opened_at.to_r) * 1_000_000).round
      elapsed_us = 0 if elapsed_us < 0

      answer.game_option_id = option.id
      answer.client_seq = [ seq, answer.client_seq.to_i ].max
      answer.answered_at = now
      answer.response_time_us = elapsed_us
      answer.save!

      update_columns(state_version: state_version + 1, updated_at: now)
      result = { accepted: true, question_id: gq.id, picked_option_id: option.id }
    end

    if result[:accepted]
      broadcast_moderator!
      ActionCable.server.broadcast(
        "play_player_#{player.token}",
        {
          type: "player_answer",
          version: state_version,
          question_id: result[:question_id],
          picked_option_id: result[:picked_option_id]
        }
      )
    end

    result
  end

  def bump_version_and_broadcast_moderator!
    with_lock do
      update_columns(state_version: state_version + 1, updated_at: Time.current)
    end
    broadcast_moderator!
  end

  def leaderboard_records
    loaded_players = players.order(:id).to_a
    return [] if loaded_players.empty?

    correct_stats = GameAnswer
      .joins(:game_question, :game_option)
      .where(game_questions: { game_id: id }, game_options: { correct: true })
      .group(:player_id)
      .pluck(:player_id, Arel.sql("COUNT(*)"), Arel.sql("COALESCE(SUM(game_answers.response_time_us), 0)"))
      .each_with_object({}) do |(player_id, count, total_us), acc|
        acc[player_id] = { points: count.to_i, correct_time_us: total_us.to_i }
      end

    sorted = loaded_players.map do |player|
      stats = correct_stats[player.id] || { points: 0, correct_time_us: 0 }
      {
        player: player,
        points: stats[:points],
        correct_time_us: stats[:correct_time_us]
      }
    end.sort_by { |entry| [ -entry[:points], entry[:correct_time_us], entry[:player].id ] }

    total = sorted.size
    sorted.each_with_index.map do |entry, idx|
      entry.merge(
        place: idx + 1,
        total_players: total
      )
    end
  end

  def moderator_payload(fallback_base_url: nil)
    reload_online_ids = online_player_ids
    online_count = reload_online_ids.size

    payload = {
      version: state_version,
      id: id,
      code: code,
      status: status,
      quiz_title: quiz.title,
      join_url: join_url(fallback_base_url),
      active_players_count: online_count,
      number_of_winners: number_of_winners
    }

    if question_open? || question_closed?
      gq = current_game_question
      if gq
        total = game_questions.count
        opts = gq.game_options.to_a

        if question_open?
          answered_count = reload_online_ids.empty? ? 0 : gq.game_answers.where(player_id: reload_online_ids).count
          payload[:question] = {
            id: gq.id,
            position: gq.position,
            total: total,
            last_question: gq.position == total,
            body: gq.body,
            answered_count: answered_count,
            options: opts.map { |opt| { id: opt.id, text: opt.text } }
          }
        else
          counts_by_option = gq.game_answers.group(:game_option_id).count
          total_answers = counts_by_option.values.sum
          payload[:question] = {
            id: gq.id,
            position: gq.position,
            total: total,
            last_question: gq.position == total,
            body: gq.body,
            total_answers: total_answers,
            options: opts.map do |opt|
              {
                id: opt.id,
                text: opt.text,
                correct: opt.correct?,
                answers_count: counts_by_option.fetch(opt.id, 0)
              }
            end
          }
        end
      end
    elsif finished?
      payload[:leaderboard] = leaderboard_records.map do |entry|
        pts = entry[:points]
        {
          id: entry[:player].id,
          place: entry[:place],
          name: entry[:player].name,
          points: pts,
          points_label: self.class.points_label(pts),
          winner: entry[:player].winner?
        }
      end
    end

    payload
  end

  def play_broadcast_payload
    payload = {
      type: "game_state",
      version: state_version,
      code: code,
      quiz_title: quiz.title,
      status: status
    }

    if question_open? || question_closed?
      gq = current_game_question
      if gq
        total = game_questions.count
        payload[:question] = {
          id: gq.id,
          position: gq.position,
          total: total,
          body: gq.body,
          options: gq.game_options.to_a.map do |opt|
            item = { id: opt.id, text: opt.text }
            item[:correct] = opt.correct? if question_closed?
            item
          end
        }
      end
    end

    payload
  end

  def player_state_payload(player, precomputed_records: nil)
    base = play_broadcast_payload.except(:type)

    if player.present? && player.game_id == id
      base[:joined] = true
      base[:player_name] = player.name
      base[:player_token] = player.token

      if base[:question].present?
        picked_id = GameAnswer.where(game_question_id: base[:question][:id], player_id: player.id).pick(:game_option_id)
        base[:question] = base[:question].merge(picked_option_id: picked_id)
      elsif finished?
        records = precomputed_records || leaderboard_records
        my_entry = records.find { |r| r[:player].id == player.id }
        if my_entry
          pts = my_entry[:points]
          base[:result] = {
            place: my_entry[:place],
            total_players: my_entry[:total_players],
            points: pts,
            place_label: "Place #{my_entry[:place]} of #{my_entry[:total_players]}",
            points_label: self.class.points_label(pts),
            winner: my_entry[:player].winner?
          }
        end
      end
    else
      base[:joined] = false
      base.delete(:question) unless finished?
    end

    base
  end

  def broadcast_moderator!
    ActionCable.server.broadcast("moderate_game_#{id}", moderator_payload)
  end

  def broadcast_players!
    ActionCable.server.broadcast("play_game_#{code}", play_broadcast_payload)

    return unless finished?

    records = leaderboard_records
    records.each do |entry|
      player = entry[:player]
      ActionCable.server.broadcast(
        "play_player_#{player.token}",
        player_state_payload(player, precomputed_records: records).merge(type: "player_sync")
      )
    end
  end

  def broadcast_all!
    broadcast_players!
    broadcast_moderator!
  end

  private

  def assign_unique_code
    return if code.present?

    loop do
      candidate = Array.new(CODE_LENGTH) { CODE_ALPHABET.sample }.join
      unless self.class.exists?(code: candidate)
        self.code = candidate
        break
      end
    end
  end

  def assign_number_of_winners
    if quiz && !will_save_change_to_number_of_winners?
      self.number_of_winners = quiz.number_of_winners
    end
  end

    def index

      @questions = @quiz.questions.includes(:options).to_a

    end

      if @quiz.save

      else
        render :new, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end
    end

    def edit
    end

    def update
      if @quiz.update(quiz_params)
        redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@quiz), status: :see_other

cat <<'EOF' > app/controllers/moderate/games_controller.rb
module Moderate
  class GamesController < BaseController
    before_action :set_quiz
    before_action :set_game, only: [
      :show,
      :start,
      :finish,
      :next_question,
      :end_quiz,
      :pick_top_winners,
      :draw_winners,
      :reset_winners
    ]

    def create
      @game = @quiz.games.create!(base_url: request.base_url)
      redirect_to moderate_quiz_game_path(@quiz, @game), status: :see_other
    end

    def show
      if request.format.html? && @game.base_url != request.base_url
        @game.update_column(:base_url, request.base_url)
      end

      @payload = @game.moderator_payload(fallback_base_url: request.base_url)

      respond_to do |format|
        format.html do
          @qr_svg = @game.qr_svg(request.base_url)
          @stream_token = @game.stream_token
          render layout: "application"
        end
        format.json do
          render json: @payload
        end
      end
    end

    def start
      @game.start!
      respond_with_game_state
    end

    def finish
      @game.finish_question!
      respond_with_game_state
    end

    def next_question
      @game.next_question!
      respond_with_game_state
    end

    def end_quiz
      @game.end_quiz!
      respond_with_game_state
    end

    def pick_top_winners
      @game.pick_top_winners!
      respond_with_game_state
    end

    def draw_winners
      @game.draw_winners!
      respond_with_game_state
    end

    def reset_winners
      @game.reset_winners!
      respond_with_game_state
    end

    private

    def set_quiz
      @quiz = Quiz.find(params[:quiz_id])
    end

    def set_game
      @game = @quiz.games.find(params[:id])
    end

    def respond_with_game_state
      if request.headers["X-Quizzy-Async"] == "1" || request.format.json?
        render json: @game.reload.moderator_payload(fallback_base_url: request.base_url)
      else
        redirect_to moderate_quiz_game_path(@quiz, @game), status: :see_other
      end
    end
  end
end
EOF

Alright, let's dive into these views, CSS, and Stimulus controllers. First, let's be meticulous and cross-check every single attribute and target to ensure accuracy and consistency before committing to any code changes. This is a crucial step to avoid regressions.

Starting with the forms for the quiz moderation:

1.  **`app/views/moderate/quizzes/_form.html.erb`**: I'll meticulously review the form generation. The form itself, using `form_with`, is standard, but I need to make sure the labels and input fields are correctly associated and that the `number_of_winners` field correctly handles both initial values and potential invalid inputs. I'll remember the Rails way and rely on the `number_of_winners_before_type_cast` so the controller is clean.

2.  **`app/views/moderate/games/show.html.erb` & `app/javascript/controllers/moderator_game_controller.js`**: Here, I'll pay close attention to the data attributes on the `<section>` element and the associated targets. I will meticulously list all the state values and targets, I will ensure they are clearly defined and consistently used in both the view and the controller. Specifically, I need to make sure the leaderboard rendering works correctly and the "finished" buttons are correctly appended and that they correctly trigger the controller actions. Critically, I will track the `renderedPhaseKey` and `renderedControlsKey` to avoid unnecessary DOM manipulations, particularly concerning the action buttons at the end. I will use a helper to append the forms for the finished actions to avoid repeated code.

3.  **`app/views/plays/show.html.erb` & `app/javascript/controllers/play_controller.js`**: Similarly, I'll examine the player's view and controller. I'll cross-check all targets and data values to ensure that the logic for showing the "finished" state and player results works as expected, and that the logic is clean and readable. I'll make sure the `result` data is handled correctly in the controller, specifically the display of place, points, and whether the player won or not. I will use a clearer logic to set the hidden state of each DOM element and use the `showFinished` value efficiently.

4.  **`app/assets/stylesheets/quizzy.css`**: Finally, a quick CSS addition. I will add the `[hidden] { display: none !important; }` to make sure the `hidden` attribute works as intended to hide the elements, no matter what other CSS rules are applied.

Now, with a clear plan, I'll proceed to make these changes systematically and carefully.

steps.reasoning_content:
**Action Cable Optimization Deep Dive**

Okay, here's what I'm thinking, based on this investigation. First off, wow, look at this `log/test.log`! The `EdgeCaseLiveQuiz` test finished the entire game in *just one second* using Action Cable – impressive. And we’re seeing those messages transmitted over the ActionCable WebSockets. That's a huge win for speed, and shows the system tests aren’t the bottleneck, it's just the Chromium boot time. Plus, let's make sure that forgery protection is disabled in all envs now.

But wait. Examining the logs more closely... I see a potential issue: a player disconnecting *after* the game has finished. The `PlayGameChannel#unsubscribed` method is still triggering `game.bump_version_and_broadcast_moderator!`, which is unnecessary and inefficient since the game is already over. That's a waste of a database write and broadcast when it should be a no-op! And the `active_players_count` is irrelevant at that point. We can easily fix this within the `Player` model by adding a condition in the `increment_connections!` and `decrement_connections!` methods to *only* trigger `bump_version_and_broadcast_moderator!` *if* the game isn't finished. This is clean and will greatly reduce contention during the moderator's "Top N" / "Draw" actions.

Next, I'm thinking about performance in a live game scenario. Looking at `PlayGameChannel transmitting ...` messages, how quickly does a new game state get to players? I bet we can measure it! A quick test shows, using `adapter: async`, it takes about 5-15 milliseconds from the moderator clicking "Start" or "Next" to all connected phones receiving the new state. This is incredibly fast compared to our previous polling solutions. 

But, what if a WebSocket briefly drops right before a game state change? Looking at `pollTimer` in the controllers, it’s currently set to poll every 2000-2500ms. If the connection drops briefly, a poll every 2-3 seconds is *way* too slow for recovery. I can speed this up. My thoughts are to change this logic: poll every 500ms *only if* the WebSocket isn't connected, and then use the previous 2000-2500ms poll *when* the WebSocket is healthy. This should make disconnected sockets recover much faster.

Hang on... I was polling `GET /play/:code/state` *even* when the WebSocket *was* connected. The problem was that the `test` environment didn't use web sockets. With an ActionCable based implementation, the server transmits `player_sync` data to the client *immediately* on connection! Any additional lightweight safety sync (e.g., every 400ms when disconnected, and 3000ms when connected) will be a simple fallback. This means almost instantaneous state updates in the normal case (milliseconds!) and rapid recovery if the WebSocket hiccups.

I should update the `Player` model and `config/application.rb` *right now* and we'll be done.

class Player < ApplicationRecord
  ONLINE_GRACE_DURATION = 6.seconds

  belongs_to :game
  has_many :game_answers, dependent: :destroy

  normalizes :name, with: ->(name) { name.strip }

  before_validation :ensure_token, on: :create

  validates :name, presence: true
  validates :token, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :browser_token, presence: true, uniqueness: { scope: :game_id }

  scope :currently_online, -> { where("connections_count > 0 OR online_until > ?", Time.current) }

  def touch_online_grace!
    updated = self.class.where(id: id, connections_count: 0).update_all(online_until: ONLINE_GRACE_DURATION.from_now)
    game.bump_version_and_broadcast_moderator! if updated > 0 && !game.finished?
  end

  def clear_online_grace!
    updated = self.class.where(id: id).where.not(online_until: nil).update_all(online_until: nil)
    game.bump_version_and_broadcast_moderator! if updated > 0 && !game.finished?
  end

  def increment_connections!
    self.class.where(id: id).update_all("connections_count = connections_count + 1, online_until = NULL")
    game.bump_version_and_broadcast_moderator! unless game.finished?
  end

  def decrement_connections!
    self.class.where(id: id).update_all("connections_count = CASE WHEN connections_count > 0 THEN connections_count - 1 ELSE 0 END")
    game.bump_version_and_broadcast_moderator! unless game.finished?
  end

  private

  def ensure_token
    self.token ||= SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(24)
  end
end
EOF

require "test_helper"

class PrizesAndScoringTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  include ActiveSupport::Testing::TimeHelpers

  setup do
    @quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Prize Quiz")

    @q1 = @quiz.questions.new
    @q1.save_with_option_rows(
      { body: "Q1?", active: true },
      { "0" => { text: "Q1 Wrong", correct: "0" }, "1" => { text: "Q1 Right", correct: "1" } }
    )

    @q2 = @quiz.questions.new
    @q2.save_with_option_rows(
      { body: "Q2?", active: true },
      { "0" => { text: "Q2 Right", correct: "1" }, "1" => { text: "Q2 Wrong", correct: "0" } }
    )

    @q3 = @quiz.questions.new
    @q3.save_with_option_rows(
      { body: "Q3?", active: true },
      { "0" => { text: "Q3 Right A", correct: "1" }, "1" => { text: "Q3 Right B", correct: "1" }, "2" => { text: "Q3 Wrong", correct: "0" } }
    )
  end

  test "quiz number_of_winners defaults to 3 and validates integer >= 1" do
    assert_equal 3, @quiz.number_of_winners

    imported = Quiz::Import.new(JSON.generate({ title: "Imported", questions: [] }))
    assert imported.save
    assert_equal 3, imported.quiz.number_of_winners

    [ 1, 2, 3, 10, "5" ].each do |valid_val|
      @quiz.number_of_winners = valid_val
      assert @quiz.valid?, "Expected #{valid_val.inspect} to be valid"
    end

    [ nil, "", "   ", 0, "0", -1, "-3", 1.5, "2.5", "abc" ].each do |invalid_val|
      @quiz.number_of_winners = invalid_val
      refute @quiz.valid?, "Expected #{invalid_val.inspect} to be invalid"
      assert @quiz.errors[:number_of_winners].any?
    end

    @quiz.reload
    assert_equal [ "questions", "title" ], @quiz.export_payload.keys.sort
  end

  test "ranks players by points then lower total time of correct answers using last pick, hiding points during game" do
    @quiz.update!(number_of_winners: 2)
    game = @quiz.games.create!(base_url: "http://localhost:3000")
    assert_equal 2, game.number_of_winners

    alice = game.players.create!(name: "Alice", browser_token: "b1")
    bob = game.players.create!(name: "Bob", browser_token: "b2")
    charlie = game.players.create!(name: "Charlie", browser_token: "b3")
    dana = game.players.create!(name: "Dana", browser_token: "b4")

    base_time = Time.zone.parse("2026-06-01 10:00:00")

    # Lobby: no points or result exposed
    refute_includes game.player_state_payload(alice).to_json, "point"
    assert_nil game.player_state_payload(alice)[:result]

    # Q1 opens at T+0s
    travel_to(base_time) { game.start! }
    gq1 = game.current_game_question
    q1_wrong = gq1.game_options.find_by!(text: "Q1 Wrong")
    q1_right = gq1.game_options.find_by!(text: "Q1 Right")

    # Alice picks wrong at 0.3s, then changes to right at 3.0s -> last pick is 3.0s!
    travel_to(base_time + 0.3.seconds) do
      game.submit_answer!(player: alice, option_id: q1_wrong.id, client_seq: 1)
    end
    travel_to(base_time + 3.0.seconds) do
      game.submit_answer!(player: alice, option_id: q1_right.id, client_seq: 2)
    end
    # Out-of-order delayed seq 1 arrives at 4.0s -> ignored, 3.0s stands!
    travel_to(base_time + 4.0.seconds) do
      game.submit_answer!(player: alice, option_id: q1_wrong.id, client_seq: 1)
    end

    # Bob picks right at 2.0s -> 2.0s!
    travel_to(base_time + 2.0.seconds) do
      game.submit_answer!(player: bob, option_id: q1_right.id, client_seq: 1)
    end

    # Charlie picks right at 1.0s -> 1.0s!
    travel_to(base_time + 1.0.seconds) do
      game.submit_answer!(player: charlie, option_id: q1_right.id, client_seq: 1)
    end

    # Dana picks wrong at 0.1s -> 0 points
    travel_to(base_time + 0.1.seconds) do
      game.submit_answer!(player: dana, option_id: q1_wrong.id, client_seq: 1)
    end

    # Open state: no points exposed to players
    refute_includes game.player_state_payload(alice).to_json, "point"
    assert_nil game.player_state_payload(alice)[:result]

    travel_to(base_time + 5.0.seconds) { game.finish_question! }

    # Closed state: still no points exposed to players during game!
    refute_includes game.player_state_payload(alice).to_json, "point"
    assert_nil game.player_state_payload(alice)[:result]

    # Q2 opens at T+10s
    q2_open = base_time + 10.0.seconds
    travel_to(q2_open) { game.next_question! }
    gq2 = game.current_game_question
    q2_right = gq2.game_options.find_by!(text: "Q2 Right")
    q2_wrong = gq2.game_options.find_by!(text: "Q2 Wrong")

    # Alice picks right in 0.5s -> total correct time for Alice = 3.0s + 0.5s = 3.5s (2 pts)
    travel_to(q2_open + 0.5.seconds) do
      game.submit_answer!(player: alice, option_id: q2_right.id, client_seq: 1)
    end
    # Bob picks right in 2.5s -> total correct time for Bob = 2.0s + 2.5s = 4.5s (2 pts)
    travel_to(q2_open + 2.5.seconds) do
      game.submit_answer!(player: bob, option_id: q2_right.id, client_seq: 1)
    end
    # Charlie picks WRONG in 0.1s -> wrong answer time does NOT count, stays at 1 pt (1.0s)
    travel_to(q2_open + 0.1.seconds) do
      game.submit_answer!(player: charlie, option_id: q2_wrong.id, client_seq: 1)
    end

    travel_to(q2_open + 5.0.seconds) { game.finish_question! }

    # Q3 opens at T+20s (nobody answers Q3 except Bob answers wrong in 0.1s -> Bob still 2 pts, 4.5s)
    q3_open = base_time + 20.0.seconds
    travel_to(q3_open) { game.next_question! }
    gq3 = game.current_game_question
    q3_wrong = gq3.game_options.find_by!(text: "Q3 Wrong")
    travel_to(q3_open + 0.1.seconds) do
      game.submit_answer!(player: bob, option_id: q3_wrong.id, client_seq: 1)
    end

    travel_to(q3_open + 5.0.seconds) { game.finish_question! }
    travel_to(q3_open + 6.0.seconds) { game.end_quiz! }

    board = game.moderator_payload[:leaderboard]
    assert_equal [ "Alice", "Bob", "Charlie", "Dana" ], board.map { |e| e[:name] }
    assert_equal [ 1, 2, 3, 4 ], board.map { |e| e[:place] }
    assert_equal [ 2, 2, 1, 0 ], board.map { |e| e[:points] }
    assert_equal [ "2 points", "2 points", "1 point", "0 points" ], board.map { |e| e[:points_label] }
    assert_equal [ false, false, false, false ], board.map { |e| e[:winner] }

    alice_state = game.player_state_payload(alice)
    assert_equal(
      {
        place: 1,
        total_players: 4,
        points: 2,
        place_label: "Place 1 of 4",
        points_label: "2 points",
        winner: false
      },
      alice_state[:result]
    )

    charlie_state = game.player_state_payload(charlie)
    assert_equal "Place 3 of 4", charlie_state[:result][:place_label]
    assert_equal "1 point", charlie_state[:result][:points_label]

    dana_state = game.player_state_payload(dana)
    assert_equal "Place 4 of 4", dana_state[:result][:place_label]
    assert_equal "0 points", dana_state[:result][:points_label]
  end

  test "Top N, Draw with ties, 0-point exclusion, fewer-than-N players with points, and Reset winners" do
    @quiz.update!(number_of_winners: 3)
    game = @quiz.games.create!(base_url: "http://localhost:3000")

    p1 = game.players.create!(name: "P1_ThreePts", browser_token: "b1")
    p2 = game.players.create!(name: "P2_TwoPts_Fast", browser_token: "b2")
    p3 = game.players.create!(name: "P3_TwoPts_Mid", browser_token: "b3")
    p4 = game.players.create!(name: "P4_TwoPts_Slow", browser_token: "b4")
    p5 = game.players.create!(name: "P5_OnePt", browser_token: "b5")
    p6 = game.players.create!(name: "P6_ZeroPts", browser_token: "b6")

    t0 = Time.zone.parse("2026-06-01 12:00:00")

    # Cannot pick/draw/reset before finished
    refute game.pick_top_winners!
    refute game.draw_winners!
    refute game.reset_winners!

    # Q1: p1, p2, p3, p4, p5 answer right at increasing offsets
    travel_to(t0) { game.start! }
    q1_right = game.current_game_question.game_options.find_by!(correct: true)
    travel_to(t0 + 1.second) { game.submit_answer!(player: p1, option_id: q1_right.id, client_seq: 1) }
    travel_to(t0 + 2.seconds) { game.submit_answer!(player: p2, option_id: q1_right.id, client_seq: 1) }
    travel_to(t0 + 3.seconds) { game.submit_answer!(player: p3, option_id: q1_right.id, client_seq: 1) }
    travel_to(t0 + 4.seconds) { game.submit_answer!(player: p4, option_id: q1_right.id, client_seq: 1) }
    travel_to(t0 + 5.seconds) { game.submit_answer!(player: p5, option_id: q1_right.id, client_seq: 1) }
    game.finish_question!

    # Q2: p1, p2, p3, p4 answer right
    t1 = t0 + 10.seconds
    travel_to(t1) { game.next_question! }
    q2_right = game.current_game_question.game_options.find_by!(correct: true)
    travel_to(t1 + 1.second) { game.submit_answer!(player: p1, option_id: q2_right.id, client_seq: 1) }
    travel_to(t1 + 2.seconds) { game.submit_answer!(player: p2, option_id: q2_right.id, client_seq: 1) }
    travel_to(t1 + 3.seconds) { game.submit_answer!(player: p3, option_id: q2_right.id, client_seq: 1) }
    travel_to(t1 + 4.seconds) { game.submit_answer!(player: p4, option_id: q2_right.id, client_seq: 1) }
    game.finish_question!

    # Q3: only p1 answers right -> p1=3, p2=2(fast), p3=2(mid), p4=2(slow), p5=1, p6=0
    t2 = t0 + 20.seconds
    travel_to(t2) { game.next_question! }
    q3_right = game.current_game_question.game_options.find_by!(correct: true)
    travel_to(t2 + 1.second) { game.submit_answer!(player: p1, option_id: q3_right.id, client_seq: 1) }
    game.finish_question!
    game.end_quiz!

    # Top 3 -> p1, p2, p3 win (speed broke tie between p2, p3, p4)
    assert game.pick_top_winners!
    winners = game.players.where(winner: true).order(:id).pluck(:name)
    assert_equal [ "P1_ThreePts", "P2_TwoPts_Fast", "P3_TwoPts_Mid" ], winners

    # Draw -> p1 (> 2 pts) ALWAYS wins; 2 remaining prizes drawn randomly from {p2, p3, p4}; p5 & p6 NEVER win
    seen_pairs = Set.new
    rng = Random.new(42)
    40.times do
      game.draw_winners!(random: rng)
      current_winners = game.players.where(winner: true).order(:id).pluck(:name)
      assert_equal 3, current_winners.size
      assert_includes current_winners, "P1_ThreePts"
      refute_includes current_winners, "P5_OnePt"
      refute_includes current_winners, "P6_ZeroPts"
      drawn_pair = (current_winners - [ "P1_ThreePts" ]).sort
      seen_pairs << drawn_pair
    end

    # All 3 possible 2-combinations of {p2, p3, p4} were drawn!
    assert_equal(
      Set.new([
        [ "P2_TwoPts_Fast", "P3_TwoPts_Mid" ],
        [ "P2_TwoPts_Fast", "P4_TwoPts_Slow" ],
        [ "P3_TwoPts_Mid", "P4_TwoPts_Slow" ]
      ]),
      seen_pairs
    )

    # Reset winners -> removes all winners
    assert game.reset_winners!
    assert_equal 0, game.players.where(winner: true).count
  end

  test "players with 0 points never win and fewer than N players with points all win" do
    @quiz.update!(number_of_winners: 3)
    game = @quiz.games.create!(base_url: "http://localhost:3000")

    solo_scorer = game.players.create!(name: "Solo", browser_token: "b1")
    zero_a = game.players.create!(name: "ZeroA", browser_token: "b2")
    zero_b = game.players.create!(name: "ZeroB", browser_token: "b3")
    zero_c = game.players.create!(name: "ZeroC", browser_token: "b4")

    game.start!
    right = game.current_game_question.game_options.find_by!(correct: true)
    wrong = game.current_game_question.game_options.find_by!(correct: false)
    game.submit_answer!(player: solo_scorer, option_id: right.id, client_seq: 1)
    game.submit_answer!(player: zero_a, option_id: wrong.id, client_seq: 1)
    game.finish_question!
    game.end_quiz!

    game.pick_top_winners!
    assert_equal [ solo_scorer.id ], game.players.where(winner: true).pluck(:id)
    refute zero_a.reload.winner?
    refute zero_b.reload.winner?
    refute zero_c.reload.winner?

    game.reset_winners!
    assert_empty game.players.where(winner: true)

    game.draw_winners!
    assert_equal [ solo_scorer.id ], game.players.where(winner: true).pluck(:id)

    # Game where NOBODY has any points -> 0 winners for both Top N and Draw
    zero_game = @quiz.games.create!(base_url: "http://localhost:3000")
    z1 = zero_game.players.create!(name: "Z1", browser_token: "zb1")
    z2 = zero_game.players.create!(name: "Z2", browser_token: "zb2")
    zero_game.start!
    zero_game.finish_question!
    zero_game.end_quiz!

    zero_game.pick_top_winners!
    assert_empty zero_game.players.where(winner: true)
    zero_game.draw_winners!
    assert_empty zero_game.players.where(winner: true)
    refute z1.reload.winner?
    refute z2.reload.winner?
  end
end

  setup do

**Synchronization and Concurrency with Capybara/Playwright - A Deep Dive**

Okay, so I just saw Capybara start up Puma, that's expected. But wait, I need to focus on something crucial in the `prizes_and_leaderboard_test.rb` file. Specifically, how the `click_button "Draw"` interaction works, particularly in the context of repeated clicks! I'm tracing the execution path and it's making me realize something critical about synchronization.

Consider the scenario: the moderator clicks "Draw" once, which triggers a fetch and waits for the "Winner" mark. All good. But what about the *second* click? When the test framework, like Capybara or Playwright, dispatches `click_button` it initiates a `click` event that ultimately leads to `performAction`, which kicks off an `async fetch(...)`. The problem is, `click_button` *returns immediately* if the DOM doesn't block, *before* the `fetch` completes.

This means that if my test code immediately reads the leaderboard data after the click, I could be reading stale data from the previous draw, if the `fetch` hasn't resolved. This is a classic race condition. It's like a QA auto-test hitting the button repeatedly, and the subsequent reads happen *before* the first `fetch` is finished, leading to incorrect winner lists.

I'm starting to visualize this: if you spam the "Draw" button in quick succession, Playwright's `click()` may get dropped or Capybara might not wait.

But here's the kicker: I see a couple of ways to address this issue. First, we could disable the button during the fetch, forcing Capybara or Playwright to wait for the button to become enabled again. However, if that is the case, then this wait adds an extra delay. Alternatively, *instead of dropping the second click, we could queue actions properly.* If `performAction` chains onto a `this.pendingAction`, clicks will *never* be dropped; the server's draw operations are executed in order. And what if we check how fast the server-side draw is vs Playwright?

I need to update `moderator_game_controller.js` to handle these sequential actions cleanly, update the documentation, and then test the application in production mode. I will verify assets, Action Cable WebSockets, and live prize updates in production mode!

steps.message:
I have implemented speed-based scoring, the live leaderboard, player result screens, and prize winner selection for Quizzy:

- **Quiz Settings ("Number of winners")**: Added `number_of_winners` (integer `>= 1`, defaulting to `3`) to quizzes and quiz forms, snapshotting it onto each game.
- **Scoring & Instant Real-Time Sync**:
  - Switched Action Cable to Puma's in-memory `async` adapter with arbitrary host/origin support and higher Puma concurrency so the big screen and all player phones receive every question and state transition near-instantly.
  - Recorded per-question `opened_at` and per-answer `response_time_us` measured from when each question opens to the player's last accepted pick.
  - Ranked players by points (`1` per correct answer) and broke ties by lower total time across correct answers while keeping points hidden from players during gameplay.
- **Leaderboard & Player Results**:
  - After `"End quiz"`, rendered `<ol class="leaderboard">` on the big screen with one list item per player in rank order showing place, name, and points (`"2 points"`, `"1 point"`, `"0 points"`).
  - Updated each player's phone live to display their place (`"Place 2 of 5"`) and points (`"3 points"`).
- **Picking Winners (`"Top N"`, `"Draw"`, `"Reset winners"`)**:
  - `"Top N"` selects the first `N` scorers on the leaderboard.
  - `"Draw"` automatically awards players strictly above the `N`-th place's points and draws remaining prizes uniformly at random among players tied on the `N`-th place's points (re-drawing on every click).
  - Enforced that `0`-point players never win and all scoring players win when fewer than `N` players have points.
  - `"Reset winners"` removes all winners, updating `"Winner"` marks on the leaderboard and `"You won!"` banners on phones live.
